items.title: Ira Gitler interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: a riff that was used behind Trummy Young’s vocal of “Margie” with Jimmie Lunceford

ctx.x: Well that didn’t explain any jazz harmonies though.

No, no, it just was for technique. No. I think he listened and he heard, and most of the great musicians, no matter how much training they have and put that in their service, it’s the intuitive and what they soak up and play back at you. You know Charlie Parker was amazing the way he would hear fragments of songs or whole songs, and incorporate them. He just was omnivorous in his listening, you could see. And an incredible retentive memory, as we know from the way he would change his solos from take to take on a…
But it kind of has that semi-classical as we used to call it, light opera or whatever, it’s a theme like that. And he plays that and does a lot of miraculous things with it.
